chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on one of his journeys, he met a group of riders. They said, 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'Who are you?' They said, 'We are believers, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'So what is the reality of your faith?' They said, 'Contentment with the decree of Allah, delegation to Allah, and submission to the command of Allah.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Scholars, wise ones, who almost could be from the wisdom of the Prophets. If you are truthful, do not build what you will not dwell in, and do not amass what you will not consume, and fear Allah, to Whom you will be returning.'
ai.seo_question: What is the true reality of faith according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) identifies true faith as complete contentment with divine decree (Rida) and submission to God's will, elevating such believers to the status of wise scholars. He then links this spiritual conviction to practical asceticism, advising against hoarding wealth or property that one cannot immediately utilize, thereby emphasizing detachment from worldly accumulation. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that genuine Iman necessitates both internal spiritual alignment and external behavioral simplicity.
